answer: An opal shows a different face to each viewer, so trust cannot rest on one account. Each identity needs two holders outside its own ledge to countersign its claim, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate witnesses rather than a single ring. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. An audit re-walks a random dune each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim forfeits its bond, which cannot be pooled or resold.
